messages:
maya: heads-up — planning to publish SDK updates in ~30m: Python v1.4.0 (breaking: sync client deprecated) and TS v0.9.3 (canary). Will post release notes + migration guide.
publish-bot: build 789 queued for py-sdk@1.4.0 and ts-sdk@0.9.3-canary. CI checks started.
sophie: quick q — we're still in the 5-6pm PST change window right? last-minute deps ok? :eyes:
alan: yep window open. just a heads-up: I saw a streaming edge-case in py where `chunked=True` + `timeout` returns truncated messages. small repro: `pytest tests/test_stream.py::test_chunked_timeout -k truncated`
kevin: repro'd locally. stack: `service/streaming.py:142` -> `decode_chunk` -> IndexError on empty chunk. throwing a fix now but it's not trivial.
maya: hmm. options: 1) delay both releases until fix merges, 2) publish Py (non-streaming paths) and hold TS canary, 3) publish Py but pin wheels to drop streaming flag until patch. Thoughts?
sophie: I prefer minimal blast radius — publish only what's safe. can we publish py without enabling the new streaming flag by default?
alan: yes we can gate it behind `enable_stream_v2` flag in config. released wheels can default to false. that avoids hotfix.
kevin: will still open PR for fix (WIP) but gating is fastest. also keep TS as canary only.
publish-bot: npm publish job queued for ts-sdk@0.9.3-canary (dry-run).
maya: decision: publish Python v1.4.0 with `enable_stream_v2=false` in defaults, tag the release with "deprecate-sync-client" note. hold TS under canary and DO NOT promote to stable until kevin's streaming fix lands + e2e. rollback plan: if error rate or 5xx spike > 3% for 10m, revert wheels and pin previous version.
sophie: I'll update release notes: explain deprecation timeline for sync client, include migration steps (async usage + example snippet), and add note that TS will remain canary. will also add audit entry in console.
kevin: PR #3125 opened for streaming fix, adding unit + e2e. targeting hotfix merge in next 2 hours. will ping here.
maya: publish timeline: will trigger py publish in 20m after ops run through checklist. @deploy-bot can you hold TS publish until I give explicit go?
deploy-bot: acknowledged. holding TS publish. scheduled py release in 18m.
alan: tagging strategy: use `1.4.0` (stable) for py, `0.9.3-canary` for ts. also add GitHub release notes pointing to migration doc: https://git.redwood/internals/sdk/migration/sync-to-async
sophie: adding changelog entries now, and will push a short customer-facing note for console banner: "Py SDK: sync client deprecated — migrate by 2026-05-01"
maya: final checks: telemetry keys, release binary signing, and docs link in release body. all good?
kevin: telemetry ok. tests green on non-streaming paths.
sophie: docs updated + changelog PR created.
publish-bot: publish started for py-sdk@1.4.0 (wheel + sdist). job 790.
publish-bot: publish succeeded for py-sdk@1.4.0 (sha256: abc123...).
maya: confirmed pip install works: `python -m pip install redwood-sdk==1.4.0` — sample app still runs with streaming opt off.
kevin: will continue to validate canary infra and e2e for streaming fix. will report back in this thread.
sophie: posting release note draft to #release-notes for review. will coordinate GA promotion of TS after kevin + e2e + perf. :thumbsup:
maya: thanks team. TS remain blocked until explicit go from me. closing loop once we have the streaming fix merged and smoke tests pass.
deploy-bot: TS publish still held.
